voiceover: Imagine you earned five hundred seventy-two dollars a week in two thousand. A dozen eggs cost ninety-one cents. Today you earn twelve hundred — but eggs cost four twenty-five. Did eggs get more expensive... or did your paycheck grow faster? <break time="500ms"/> That's the question behind what we call the Real Unit Price Index — RUPI. Take twenty-five years of Bureau of Labor Statistics prices — per pound, per gallon, per dozen — and divide each product's price growth by median wage growth.

visual.description: Split comparison card. Left side: '2000' header — '$572/week' (JetBrains Mono, Muted Pink), 'Eggs: $0.91/dozen' below. Right side: '2025' header — '$1,206/week' (JetBrains Mono, Muted Blue), 'Eggs: $4.25/dozen'. Thin vertical divider in Sage Silver. Numbers animate in with spring counters. At the 500ms break, the comparison fades and the RUPI formula builds: 'Price Growth ÷ Wage Growth = RUPI' — each term animates in sequence. BLS logo watermark bottom-right, small, at 30% opacity.

notes: This is the educational foundation scene. The concrete wage/egg comparison makes it tangible before introducing the abstract formula. Phase 1 (comparison card) holds for ~20s, then phase 2 (formula) builds for the remaining ~19s. Numbers use JetBrains Mono with tabular figures. Spring animation for counter: stiffness 100, damping 20. BLS source footnote in Inter 14px, Sage Silver, bottom-right.
